attributes.size: large cracks across FZs and HAZs

evidence.quote: Large cracks across both the FZs and HAZs can be clearly seen on the transections of the welded AC sample (see Fig. 6(a)), suggesting a poor weld-crack resistance.
Cracks with smaller sizes exist in the HAZs of the welded IFC sample (see Fig. 6(b)), implying an improved weld-crack resistance as compared to the welded AC sample.
tiny cracks with a length less than 5 m do exist in the welded FC sample, as presented under a high magnification in Fig. 6(f).
The average crack length and the crack index of the AC sample are as large as 6250±320 μm and 0.55±0.12, respectively.

the occurrence of the serrated GBs was attributed to the pinning effect of the precipitated phases, including the MC and M23C6 phases, on GBs
a low cooling rate promotes the growth of grains, but the pinning effects by the precipitated M23X6 phase and the segregation of B cause the serration of GBs

if the precipitated phase is in chain-like shape with more B segregation, continuous liquid films will form during welding due to the continuous distribution of the M23X6 phase with low melting temperatures

mechanisms.name: stress concentration relief by grain-boundary sliding

evidence.quote: the formation of continuous liquid films can relieve the stress concentration and avoid the formation of cracks, because the grains can locally glide along GBs with the aid of continuous liquid films

mechanisms.name: boron grain-boundary segregation reducing grain boundary energy

evidence.quote: the segregation of B on GBs not only promotes the formation of liquid films with a low melting temperature, but also reduces the grain boundary energy, γgb, according to the adsorption isotherm

mechanisms.name: liquid film healing and wetting improvement

evidence.quote: it will improve the wettability between the liquid films and the surfaces of grains; (2) it benefits the healing capability of the liquid films on GBs

mechanisms.name: homogeneous stress distribution by serrated grain boundaries

evidence.quote: the serrated GBs benefit a more homogenous distribution of stress in the adjacent grains [47], which is good for a better weld-crack resistance

(3) the furnace cooling (FC) with a cooling rate of ~2 °C per minutes directly from 1230 °C to the room temperature.

A good wettability between liquid films and surfaces promote the spread of the liquid films along GBs, and the good continuity of the liquid films are maintained during the local glide of grains along GBs during the cooling process of welding cycle.
Therefore, the segregation of B on GBs is another reason for the ameliorated weld-crack resistance.

This is the third reason of the engineered GBs for the amelioration of weld-crack resistance from the AC sample to the IFC and FC samples.

Due to the stress concentration and weak strength of the discontinuous liquid droplets, weld cracks often initiate at these regions and propagate along GBs [44]. This is the fundamental reason for the poor weldability of the AC sample.
